Mode for ending a debug session.

detaileddescription.para:
Cross-platform intent. Choose based on target state:
terminate: target is alive, kill it on detach
detach: target is alive, leave it running
passive: target has already exited; release session state only
Windows maps this directly to a dbgeng DEBUG_END_* flag passed to IDebugClient5::EndSession.

launch or attach request sent; waiting for first CreateProcess event.
Target is executing. Resume/step have been issued.
Target is paused at a breakpoint, step completion, or exception.
Target process has exited. Session is shutting down.
Execution lifecycle states for the debug target.

detaileddescription.para: Represents the coarse state machine of a debug session as seen by the DAP layer. Whatdbg and the engine event paths write the state. Whatdbg::run reads it.

briefdescription.para: Cause of the current stop, held as one value in State::stopReason.

detaileddescription.para:
Whatdbg::processDeferredEvents reads stopReason and runs the drain for it. Writers, by value:
none: The default. The drains set it back to none when they run. drainInitialBreak does so only after configurationDone.
initialBreak: Callbacks.cpp onBreakpoint while launching; Session_mac onProcessStateStopped while launching; Whatdbg::onAttach on macOS.
moduleLoad: Callbacks.cpp LoadModule, when no step is pending.
breakpoint: Callbacks.cpp Breakpoint; Session_mac onBreakpointStop.
step: Session::pollEvents on Windows, when no other stop is set; Session_mac onStepStop.
pause: Callbacks.cpp onBreakpoint while isPausePending; Session_mac onInterruptStop.
exception: Callbacks.cpp onBreakpoint and onUnknownException (second chance); Session_mac onSignalStop and onExceptionStop.

briefdescription.para: Return true if a symbol/variable name should be hidden from the DAP variable panel.

detaileddescription.para: Filters out compiler- and framework-injected symbols that carry no user-visible meaning: RTTI/vtable artifacts, the JUCE leak detector member, and the per-TU compile-unit-mismatch sentinel.

parameterdescription.para: Symbol or variable name as reported by the debug engine.

briefdescription.para: Extract a hexadecimal address from a debug engine value text string.

detaileddescription.para: Scans the input for a "0x" prefixed hex token and parses it as a 64-bit unsigned integer. Used to extract pointer values from formatted symbol text such as "0x0000000010db01b0 \"hello\"". Backtick digit-group padding (dbgeng's 64-bit address formatting) is stripped before parsing.

parameterdescription.para: Symbol value text that may contain a hex address.

simplesect.para: Parsed address, or 0 if no hex address is found.

briefdescription.para: Attempt to pretty-print an SBValue using its known type name.

detaileddescription.para: Dispatches to type-specific formatters for types such as juce::String and std::unique_ptr. Returns empty if the type is not recognized — callers should fall back to SBValue::GetValue() / SBValue::GetSummary().

parameterdescription.para: The SBValue to format. May be mutated by child walks.

simplesect.para: Formatted display string, or empty if the type is not recognized.

briefdescription.para: Translate a platform-native exception/signal code to a human-readable name.

detaileddescription.para: Windows: code is an NTSTATUS / SEH exception code (e.g., 0xC0000005 → "ACCESS_VIOLATION"). isMachException is always false. macOS: code is a POSIX signal number when isMachException is false, or a Mach exception type when isMachException is true (e.g., 11 → "EXC_BAD_ACCESS").

Implementations live in platform-specific files: Callbacks.cpp on Windows, Session_mac.cpp on macOS. Used by Whatdbg::drainExceptionStopped and Whatdbg::onExceptionInfo to build the DAP exceptionId field.

parameterdescription.para: State::isMachException — selects the Mach exception table on macOS.

simplesect.para: Human-readable name, or "0x<hex>" fallback if the code is not known.
